title: Symphony Health - Retainer Uplift & Region Staging Review
next_steps: Redwood to send updated amendment with 25% retainer uplift and APAC pilot add-on
SE to schedule 60-min private-deploy technical deep dive (deep perf + network test) next week
Customer to provide sample production prompt mix and 1-week traffic replay by 2025-03-28
Procurement and legal to align on amended SLA term by 2025-04-04
action_items: Nikhil Bose: Draft private deployment benchmark plan and collect target latency SLOs (due: 2025-03-24)
Marta Ruiz: Prepare amendment and pricing table reflecting retainer uplift + APAC add-on (due: 2025-03-25)
Dr. Priya Anand: Share 1-week sample traffic and key prompt templates for perf replay (due: 2025-03-28)
Leah Price: Confirm procurement gating items and initial review timeline (due: 2025-03-27)
summary: Quarterly check-in to review Symphony Health's renewal posture: customer is happy with Hosted API latency but needs predictable capacity for an upcoming product launch in APAC plus data residency concerns for parts of EU pipeline. Discussed options: retainer uplift on Dedicated capacity vs. hybrid Dedicated + Private (VPC). SE recommended a short private-deploy perf run to validate network and KV cache behaviour; AE to send amendment and pricing. Agreed next steps and owners; legal/procurement alignment pending.
topics: Current usage and burst patterns (daily tokens, P95 latency)
Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for residency and compliance
SLA, KMS/encryption, and audit log expectations
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-21 16:00 PT | Duration: ~46 minutes | Attendees: Marta (Redwood AE), Nikhil (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Anand, Carlos Mendes (CTO), Leah Price (Procurement)

[00:00] Marta: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call, then we'll go through usage, then proposed uplift.
[00:12] Carlos: Yep, Carlos here. Priya and I have about 45 minutes. Leah will join for the contract bit.
[00:18] Dr. Priya: Hi, Priya on the call. Thanks for the time.
[00:22] Leah: Leah here.
[00:26] Marta: Great. So, quick context—congrats on the pilot throughput last quarter, we've seen steady P50 but some P95 spikes during the morning batch window, Nikhil will go into technical detail. High level goal today: align on a 25% retainer uplift to cover expected product launch in May in APAC, plus discuss a small Private (VPC) pilot for the EU pipeline where residency is required.
[00:44] Carlos: Sounds good. To be blunt: our board wants predictability for cost and latency for the launch. Right now Hosted is fine, but we're nervous about capacity contended in APAC and about EU data controls for certain datasets.
[01:02] Nikhil: Totally understood. From infra telemetry, Symphony's tail latency episodes are correlated with long-sequence rerank jobs and a small number of synchronous calls that can't be batched. We have three viable approaches: increase dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), add APAC geocluster to reduce egress and cross-region RTT, or run a Private VPC for EU-sensitive traffic. We can also do hybrid routing—sensitive calls to Private, general inference to Hosted/Dedicated.
[01:30] Dr. Priya: Hybrid is attractive. But can you quantify what the retainer uplift would buy? Specifics: how many tokens per second or GPUs?
[01:38] Marta: Good question. For a 25% uplift on your current committed retainer, you get ability to sustain a steady additional throughput of roughly 40K tokens/minute with burst credits for up to 90th percentile spikes—ballpark. We should map that to your token mix.
[01:53] Carlos: Our current daily avg is ~110M tokens, peak minute around 120k tokens, and the launch projection is +30% daily. The risky piece is APAC peak hour where RTT adds 80-120ms to P95.
[02:09] Nikhil: If we activate APAC geocluster and pin a few model variants on Dedicated there, we can reduce network latency by ~60-80ms for your users in APAC. There's some lead time to provision GPUs in the APAC region though—typically 4-6 weeks for reserved nodes depending on availability.
[02:27] Dr. Priya: And the Private option—what's the onboarding like? We have KMS requirements and SOC2 audit needs.
[02:34] Nikhil: For Private (VPC), we spin up a customer-specific control plane with your VPC peering or private link. Key highlights: customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs forwarded to your SIEM, and RBAC/SSO through SAML. Lead time is usually 6-8 weeks plus network security approvals. There is more ops overhead but better residency guarantees.
[02:55] Leah: From procurement: cost aside, we need clear rollback/fallback language and SLA windows. Also want to know if this change affects existing data retention terms—any data stored in KV cache, etc.
[03:07] Marta: Good point. We'll include explicit fallback policies—automated routing to the nearest compatible model or region, and a clear data flow diagram. On KV cache: caching is ephemeral and per-tenant by default, we don't persist customer prompt text beyond short-term caching unless you opt-in to longer retention for warm-starts. We'll document the specifics.
[03:27] Carlos: Can you also confirm encryption at rest in Dedicated vs Private? We need to know where KMS keys live.
[03:33] Nikhil: In Hosted/Dedicated we manage keys in our KMS by default, but we support customer managed keys via an integration (bring your own KMS) for Dedicated and Private. For Private, keys can be owned by you and reside in your account or HSM. We'll include the KMS flow in the security pack.
[03:52] Dr. Priya: Great. On performance—Nikhil, you mentioned long-sequence reranks. Is quantization going to affect output quality for these models?
[04:00] Nikhil: There is a tradeoff. We use quantization profiles per-model; quality degradation is usually negligible for classification/rerank heads but can surface for certain generation tasks. For your rerank pipelines we recommend int8 with per-layer calibration. We'll run a short eval on your prompt set.
[04:18] Marta: That's one of the asks—we'd like a sample prompt bundle from you for a replay test. That will let us measure P95 under realistic KV cache warm-state and see the quantization impact.
[04:27] Dr. Priya: Ok we'll share a week of traffic and the top 20 prompt templates.
[04:31] Carlos: Timeline: launch is mid-May. What's realistic for APAC geocluster plus a short Private proof-of-concept in EU?
[04:39] Nikhil: If you sign the amendment this month and we start capacity provisioning immediately, APAC geocluster could be live late April/early May. Private pilot for a single VPC stack in EU could be completed in parallel but tends to land mid-May depending on your security review cadence. So it's tight but doable.
[04:58] Leah: Procurement will need a pricing table and amendment text. We also need a commitment window—are we adding to the existing retainer term or creating a mid-term amendment?
[05:08] Marta: We propose a mid-term amendment: 25% uplift to current retainer for the remainder of the term, with an APAC add-on billed monthly until renewal. We can also offer a limited-time pilot discount on the Private onboarding fees. I'll send a draft by Tuesday.
[05:22] Leah: Please include clear acceptance criteria for the pilot—what constitutes success so we can avoid open-ended invoices.
[05:28] Marta: Absolutely. Success criteria we typically propose: P95 under target (TBD), no more than X% error rate on rerank outputs, and successful KMS integration for audit logs. We'll draft specifics after the SE perf plan.
[05:41] Dr. Priya: One more technical Q: how does the smart routing handle model fallbacks if Dedicated in APAC is saturated? I need to understand user-facing latency impact.
[05:50] Nikhil: Smart routing can fallback to the nearest compatible model/version in Hosted or another region. Fallback adds network RTT plus any model latency delta; we can set per-route policies—low-latency routes won't fallback to cheaper variants unless explicit. We also support circuit-breaker thresholds so your application receives a clear 503 or queued response rather than unbounded retries.
[06:12] Carlos: That helps. Can we run a chaos test for routing failover? Simulate APAC loss and measure user-level impact.
[06:19] Nikhil: Yes, as part of the perf run we can script a failover scenario. We'll capture traces and token-level timing in Redwood Console for you.
[06:27] Dr. Priya: About observability—we want token-level cost attribution for each feature flag, and tracing hooks in our app. Is that available?
[06:34] Marta: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and trace integration (OpenTelemetry). We can also provide a short snippet for correlation IDs.
[06:43] Leah: What about audit logs retention for the EU Private pilot—how long can we retain and is there an extra charge?
[06:50] Nikhil: We offer configurable retention. Default short-term is 30 days, extended retention is available as an add-on. We'll include pricing options in the amendment.
[06:58] Carlos: One more stakeholder question: service credits if we miss the latency SLO during the launch window—how are those calculated?
[07:06] Marta: We have SLA language tied to P95 and availability for Dedicated customers. In the amendment we'll include a tailored SLO for your launch weeks with defined service credits. Leah, we'll align on the acceptable SLO numbers in the next step.
[07:18] Leah: Okay. For legal, we also need to confirm subprocessor lists and data flow for any 3rd-party telemetry exporters.
[07:26] Nikhil: We'll include the current subprocessor list and a diagram for telemetry exporters; if you need us to limit any exporters for EU traffic, that's configurable in the Private deployment.
[07:36] Dr. Priya: Are there any vendor lock-in concerns if we go Private? We aim for a path where we can fall back to our internal on-prem stack for certain sensitive requests.
[07:45] Nikhil: Hybrid is designed for that—routing policies can send sensitive calls to your internal on-prem model if latency and op readiness permit. We'll map compatibility and model artifact formats during the tech deep dive.
[07:56] Carlos: Sounds good. Marta, what's the pricing delta for the 25% uplift one-off vs extending the term for future discounts?
[08:04] Marta: Two paths: mid-term uplift (simple, covers immediate capacity) or commit to an extended term at a higher annual commit which lowers per-token cost. We'll present both structures in the amendment.
[08:14] Leah: We'll need both options to take to legal.
[08:17] Marta: Understood.
[08:19] -- (fast forward, SE details, some cross talk, slight transcription errors) --
[09:10] Nikhil: For the perf run, plan: 1) collect 1-week traffic and top prompt templates, 2) replay against a Dedicated node with int8 profiles, 3) run failover simulation, 4) produce a report with P50/P95, token cost estimate, and quality delta metrics. We expect to have preliminary results within 5 business days after replay starts.
[09:33] Dr. Priya: That's perfect. We'll anonymize PII and share the feed via secure S3.
[09:39] Marta: Great. I'll follow up with the delivery instructions.
[09:44] Carlos: Anything else we should flag? Ops-wise we need a contact for on-call during the launch weekend.
[09:50] Marta: We'll assign an on-call SE and provide escalation matrix in the amendment package.
[09:55] Leah: On procurement timeline—if we get the amendment by Tuesday and sign by the following Tuesday, is that workable for production provisioning?
[10:02] Nikhil: Yes that'll give us two weeks to kick off provisioning; APAC geocluster lead time still applies, but we can frontload some prep work.
[10:10] Dr. Priya: Ok we'll aim for that signoff cadence.
[10:14] Marta: Recap of next steps: Nikhil drafts perf plan, Marta drafts amendment + pricing, Priya provides sample traffic, Leah to coordinate procurement/legal review. We'll schedule the tech deep dive next week—I'll put a calendar hold.
[10:28] Carlos: Thanks everyone. Quick note: we'd like the pilot acceptance criteria written into the amendment to avoid ambiguity.
[10:34] Marta: Noted. We'll include concrete SLO numbers and QA gates.
[10:38] Leah: Thanks, bye.
[10:40] Dr. Priya: Bye.

(End of call)

Notes: Transcript includes occasional mis-hearings and short overlaps; speaker attribution approximated. Links shared: security pack (link placeholder), sample amendment template (internal link).
